text: rwb-case reads the account dates of a case at GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{accountId} on the rwb-source-data contract, returning contract date, last payment date and data as of, and the non-working days at GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/calendar/holidays?from={from}&to={to}, both one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream, and it reads no v_ace_* view itself.
why: The prescription date and the working-day count need another service's data, and no source publishes the account-date read of a set of linked accounts or any holiday read, so the consumed rows, the fake and the AC3 and AC6 mocks need a default.

impact: If P1 publishes another path or another shape, one consumed row, the AccountDatesClient and CalendarClient adapters and two fakes change; no schema, event or workflow change.

text: The stage-clock pause arrives as rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1 and rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1 on rwb.deviation.events.v1 from S8 in wave 2; at wave 1 the same pause and resume are reachable through the P3 case action contract, and AC10 is proved against the rwb-deviation contract mock until S8 exists.
why: AC10 is owned by this story and the deviation service is wave 2 while the assigned dependency set carries no S8 contract story, so the story needs one stated path for each wave.
read: RWB-ITG-E1028-ITG section 12.2 and flow step 11; Architecture v5 slide 42 (event 06 and 07); Template and Rules R5.4
confirm: Solution architect with the S8 owner and the wave 1 harness owner before the story's Done.
impact: If S8 publishes another event name or another key, one consumed row, the DeviationSignalRouter and one fixture change; the prescription clock is unaffected in every case.

text: The Timer resource carries escalatedToRole as an optional role code of up to 30 characters and escalatedAt as an optional date-time, both written by the timer story and mapped to timer.escalated_to_role and timer.escalated_at; the rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1 payload carries caseId, caseNo, timerId, timerType, expiresAt and escalateTo with caseId as the key and no personal data, and both are additive within major version 1.
why: The TSD timer table and the logical model have no row for the two escalation values and the catalogue gives no payload field list, so the baseline cannot publish a schema without a default.
read: TSD P3 v3 T3.1; legacy RWB-E1-028 section 12 (TimerBreached EV-19); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42; RWB-P3-E2015-APP section 11
confirm: Solution architect and the data steward in the baseline review, and the P7 owner for the record reference.
impact: A type, length or payload change is one schema change inside major version 1 and one regenerated type set; no table, event topic or workflow change.

text: The four operational values are provisional until UAT: the worker-poll alert fires when no poll of rwb-case is seen for 2 minutes, the catch-up alert fires when a timer stayed unmet 10 minutes after the worker returned, TimerBreached volume alerts when the hourly count leaves the trailing 7-day band by more than 3 times, and the MSG-P7-003 rate alerts above 1% of timer fires over 15 minutes.
why: The deployment cannot ship without a poll window, a catch-up window, a band and a rate, and no source gives any of them; each stays a values-file entry and never code.

confirm: DevOps lead with the rwb-case service owner at UAT, and the platform observability owner for the band definition.
impact: A threshold change is a values-file change and one runbook line; no code, contract or schema change.
